title: Evals gating for tiered batching default changes + automated rollback signals
creator: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
description:
We are introducing workload-aware batching defaults via 3 tiers (fast/standard/cost-efficient). Any change to tier defaults (global, per-model-family, per-GPU-SKU) must be gated on a repeatable prompt-set evaluation to prevent silent quality regressions, and must have clearly-defined rollback signals that SRE + release tooling can act on during staged rollout.

This ticket implements:
1) an eval gate (CI + manual release checklist) that compares candidate batching defaults vs baseline using the Workload Corpus v1 prompt-sets, and
2) a set of automated rollback signals wired to the rollout/canary tooling so we can pause/ramp down on statistically meaningful quality regressions or correlated reliability issues.

Non-goals (this ticket): invent new eval methodology for model changes; bespoke per-customer gating; long-term automated policy learning. Keep it pragmatic, auditable, and fast enough to run on every default change PR.

Background context:
- Batching changes can shift timing and token cadence; streaming partials can look different even when final outputs are similar.
- Some regressions show up only for long-context or tool-call formatting.
- We need a gate that is robust to sampling variance and produces a pass/fail summary that release engineering can trust.

Primary stakeholders:
- Applied ML/Evals: Jonas Weber (DRI), Dr. Maya Srinivasan (sponsor), Hassan Mirza (guardrails + unit economics)
- Runtime: Sofia Ivanova (scheduling), Omar El-Sayed (KV cache + batching), Marcus Reed
- SRE/Release: Rafael Mendes, Connor O'Brien

Acceptance criteria:
- A documented eval suite exists for “batching default change” that:
  - runs against Workload Corpus v1 subsets covering: short prompts, medium chat, long-context, structured/tool-call, and streaming chat traces.
  - emits a machine-readable summary artifact (json + markdown) with per-prompt-set deltas and pass/fail.
  - has stable runtime (target <= 45 min for the standard gate on a fixed GPU pool; optional extended gate can be slower).
- Pass/fail thresholds are explicit, with rationale, and approved by Applied ML + SRE:
  - Output-quality checks: distributional similarity + task-specific scoring where we have it (see “Quality metrics” below).
  - Streaming cadence checks: ensure first-token latency and per-token cadence don’t regress beyond tier allowances for fast/standard.
  - Formatting/tool-call checks: invalid JSON / invalid tool-call schema rates do not increase above threshold.
- Rollback signals are defined and wired into staged rollout playbooks:
  - When a rollout is ramping (percentage enablement), the system auto-triggers a pause/rollback recommendation (and can auto-rollback where supported) if signals breach thresholds for N consecutive windows.
  - Signals include both quality metrics (from A/B sampling) and reliability metrics (timeouts/cancels/queue delay) to catch “quality is fine but users are failing”.
- Pre-merge requirement: any PR touching tier default parameters or tier mapping tables must either:
  - attach a passing eval artifact from the gate, or
  - be explicitly labeled “no-eval-needed” with a justification and reviewer sign-off (Jonas + Sofia).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define the gate surfaces
- Identify the change points that require gating:
  - model registry tier defaults updates (per model family / GPU SKU)
  - runtime default parameter tables (tier mapping)
  - scheduler refactors that change batch formation behavior
- Add a lightweight metadata marker in PR template / CI job selection to classify “default-change” vs “non-default-change”.

2) Build/extend eval runner configuration
- Use the Workload Corpus v1 definition as source of truth for prompt sets and sampling.
- Add an eval config “batching_defaults_gate.yaml” (location TBD in evals repo) with:
  - fixed random seeds
  - fixed decoding params (temperature/top_p) per prompt set to reduce variance
  - dual-mode evaluation for streaming prompts: capture partial stream for cadence metrics + final text for quality metrics

3) Quality metrics and thresholds
- For each prompt set type:
  - General chat/text: similarity checks (e.g., embedding cosine vs baseline + length delta constraints) + “must-not-break” checks (toxicity policy doesn’t spike, empty outputs, repeated tokens).
  - Long-context: ensure response relevance heuristics don’t degrade (baseline similarity) and truncation/early-stop doesn’t increase.
  - Tool-call / structured output: schema validity rate, JSON parse rate, required fields present.
  - Rerank/embeddings (if included in corpus): ensure numeric outputs within tolerance.
- Proposed initial thresholds (to finalize in review):
  - Invalid structured output rate: +0.25% absolute max, or +25% relative (whichever is stricter), per set.
  - Empty response / degenerate loops: no increase above +0.10% absolute.
  - Similarity: median cosine similarity >= 0.985 and p10 >= 0.965 for general sets (tune after first baseline run).
  - Length deltas: median length delta within ±7% for general sets; long-context within ±10%.
- Statistical policy:
  - Use paired comparisons where possible (same prompt, same seed) and require significance for borderline cases.
  - For small sets: default to “needs human review” instead of auto-fail if confidence is low.

4) Rollback signals (runtime + dashboards)
- Define and document “rollback-worthy” signals tied to the rollout flag (tiered batching enablement) with per-tier interpretation.
- Quality rollback signals (from A/B sampling where available):
  - Structured output validity rate drop beyond threshold.
  - Increase in user-visible “tool-call parse errors” (where instrumented) correlated with tier enablement.
  - Increase in downstream “customer retry” patterns (if we have a proxy metric).
- Reliability rollback signals (from ENG-18422 metrics + existing SRE metrics):
  - p95 latency regression beyond tier’s allowed regression (SRE-defined) for 2 consecutive 10-min windows during ramp.
  - timeout rate, cancel rate: +X% relative (finalize with SRE) with minimum request volume guard.
  - queue_delay_ms p95: exceeds guardrail AND correlates with increased timeouts.
- Wire these signals into rollout tooling hooks (coordinate with Benji Okafor / Marissa Cole / Rafael Mendes):
  - “auto-pause ramp” on first breach; “auto-rollback” on sustained breach.

5) Documentation + reviewer guidance
- Update the batching-defaults quality guardrails doc to include:
  - how to run the gate locally
  - how to interpret failures
  - what labels allow bypass and who can approve
- Add a “Release checklist” snippet for Connor O’Brien + SRE on what artifacts are required for ramp approval.

Open questions:
- Do we treat streaming partial-output differences as “quality” or only as cadence/perf? Current proposal: cadence is a hard gate for fast tier; text similarity is a soft gate with a reviewer override path.
- Where do we store gate artifacts for auditability for Private/enterprise change management? Proposal: CI uploads to build artifacts + links posted to the Linear ticket and PR.
- Minimum sample sizes per prompt set: need a pragmatic default that fits time budget.

Risks:
- False positives due to sampling variability: mitigate with fixed seeds, paired prompts, and “needs review” bucket.
- False negatives if similarity metrics miss task regressions: mitigate with structured-output validity + canary A/B sampling + rollback signals.

Deliverables:
- A reproducible gate job in CI that runs on “default-change” PRs
- An eval report template (markdown) + machine-readable summary
- Defined rollback thresholds and mapping to rollout tooling actions
- Updated Confluence guardrails + reviewer guidelines
comments: 2025-02-10 (Jonas Weber): Drafted proposed thresholds for structured output validity + similarity metrics. Biggest unknown is streaming partial differences; proposing to gate cadence separately. Will sync with Sofia + Rafael.

2025-02-12 (Sofia Ivanova): +1 on separating cadence gate from text similarity for streaming. We already saw fast-tier decode prioritization changes affect partials without meaningfully changing final text.

2025-02-14 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure rollback signals have minimum-volume guards; otherwise low-traffic regions will flap. Also want explicit mapping: which metric -> auto-pause vs auto-rollback.

2025-02-19 (Hassan Mirza): Add a check for output length inflation—cost-efficient tier should not silently increase avg completion tokens (unit economics). Suggest median completion tokens delta threshold per set.

2025-02-25 (Connor O'Brien): For runtime-1.21 branch cut, we need a deterministic “pass/fail” summary to attach to release approval email. If a run is in “needs review”, who signs off and where is it recorded?

2025-03-03 (Jonas Weber): Implemented initial report format (md + json) in eval harness branch. Runtime target is ~38 min for standard gate on A100 pool. Next: integrate into perf-canary pipeline and add bypass label semantics.

2025-03-11 (Dr. Maya Srinivasan): Reviewed thresholds; approve initial values as starting point with plan to tune after first 2 weeks of beta. Please ensure we record baseline artifacts for audit trail.

2025-03-18 (Jonas Weber): Added proposal for rollback: structured validity -0.5% absolute triggers auto-pause; -1.0% triggers auto-rollback (with volume guard). Waiting on SRE confirmation for timeout/cancel thresholds.
